parsed.explanation: The combined regime couples a hostile national layer with a comparatively restrained division. Visitor-facing exposures: a February 2025 consular cable instructing refusal where records cast doubt on sex (fraud finding possible, never automatic), prompting advisories from eight-plus foreign governments; a federal bar on trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities; documented federal and immigration-custody harm (conversion-therapy-style policies, forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse); no statewide public-accommodations protection and a state hate-crime statute excluding gender identity; transition care barred for visiting minors. The division criminalises nothing, repealed its 2017 facility law, and local ordinances cover roughly 30% of the population. Litigation is active with some injunctions. No criminalisation or documented street targeting, but institutional exposure plus thin recourse holds it in elevated risk.

entry_documents.exposure: The February 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on sex, and to consider a fraud ground carrying possible lifetime ineligibility; foreign governments issued travel advisories for trans citizens over identity-document and data rules.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid to expiry; the fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; the passport restriction remains under active national litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, fraud inquiry and detention, which routes the traveller into the hostile federal custody regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections adopt conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cut, hormones removed, substituted psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; the division bars state funds for transition care for people in prison.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. The corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025 and no visitor-specific custody remedy appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document refusal or visa dispute is the most plausible route by which a foreign trans visitor enters this custody exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities, reaching federal buildings in this division. The division has no facility ban and no criminalisation (2016 law repealed 30 March 2017), but a bathroom bill was revived in 2025 and only about 30% of the population lives under a local gender-identity ordinance.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No division facility statute or offence currently bars congruent use; the earlier law was repealed after litigation and boycotts.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A local ordinance may protect in the largest city or one county, but cannot displace the federal single-sex facility rule inside federal buildings there.

care_services.exposure: Three veto-overridden laws effective 16 August 2023 bar puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s, so a visiting trans minor cannot obtain refills; a sports ban applies to visiting athletes; amended division certificates must keep displaying originally assigned sex.
care_services.protection: A 2008 designated-visitor statute supports hospital visitation. Adult emergency care is not documented as refused.
care_services.interaction: National orders framing minors' care as 'mutilation' reinforce the division ban for a travelling family.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism language targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; official orders describe trans care as mutilation; 2025 polling shows 66% support for listing assigned sex on documents; the division has a history of emergency-session restriction and a revived 2025 bathroom bill.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The dossier states ideology was never a reward criterion and counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; the national justice department previously sued this division over its discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing lowers the practical quality of local police responses where the division offers no statewide recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling trans minor cannot access transition care in the division and a parent's own trans status may invite scrutiny; federal orders direct law enforcement attention to facilitating a minor's social transition, aimed at schools rather than visitors.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented beyond the general federal hate-crime statute and ordinary parental authority; no visitor-specific protection for families appears.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care denial plus document scrutiny at entry is the operative sequence for an adult travelling with a trans minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The division hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so a bias assault lacks state bias enhancement. Published killings of 3.0 per 100k trans women are an acknowledged undercount with no general-homicide comparison, so magnitude is unusable in either direction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A national hate-crime statute covers gender identity and national employment discrimination is prohibited; no pattern of street targeting of visitors is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor must rely on federal charging or ordinary assault counts; state bias prosecution is unavailable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodations, housing or private-employment protection; county application of the amended-certificate rule is unknown; the 2025 bathroom bill's text and status and local enforcement practice are not established; no visitor-specific service-prevalence survey exists.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation with several orders enjoined, a legal-aid passport FAQ, local ordinances covering gender identity in the largest city and one county, and functioning federal courts.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical recourse depends on city or county and on which national measures are in force at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this dossier: Veluna imposes a birth-sex toilet rule on all public buildings upheld by courts with complaints routinely rejected, plus birth-sex ward placement. Our division has no facility ban or criminalisation and has repealed its statute, but adds a border refusal instruction, documented custody conversion-therapy practice and no statewide service protection, so it sits slightly above.

Closest match. Kelora's binding birth-sex custody rule with repeated documented humiliation and oversight findings that change nothing parallels the federal conversion-therapy custody policy, no transition care in division custody, and a corrections bureau that stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. Like Kelora, outside-custody life is largely ordinary, giving a similar placement.

Higher than this dossier: Teravi's problems are recurring service refusals with mediators securing readmissions and convictions, and explicitly no compulsory birth-sex placement rule. Here the custody and border-document exposures are documented state practice, and the division supplies no service remedy, so this rates below 0.55-B.

Materially higher: Ilvora combines accepted foreign documents, an enforced dead-letter statute, community acceptance and compensation ordered for a lodging refusal. Ours has active entry screening with refusal instructions, foreign travel advisories, federal facility exclusion and documented custody harm, placing it well below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: hostile national rules on entry documents and single-sex facilities plus documented federal and immigration-custody harm, layered on a division that criminalises nothing and repealed its facility law but offers no statewide service protection and no state hate-crime coverage for gender identity. Litigation, federal hate-crime law and local ordinances provide partial recourse for some encounters in some cities; they do not reach the border, federal buildings or custody, where the state's own institutions are the enforcing party. Care for a visiting minor is unavailable. Absence of criminalisation and of documented street targeting of visitors keeps the rating out of high risk, but universal entry friction, institutional custody exposure and thin service recourse hold it firmly in elevated risk.
